answer: Each epoch a fresh gale sweeps the horizon: a random seed no one can predict before it opens. Every identity must solve one sequential puzzle chained from that seed and sign it with its own quill, ninety seconds of sequential work that cannot be split across cores or precomputed. An honest agent pays ninety seconds once, and any peer verifies the result with one hash. An attacker with a thousand fakes must run a thousand ninety-second chains inside the same horizon, twenty-five hours of sequential work or a thousand cores at once, so the flood's cost grows linearly and drowns any gain.
